group:paper-mock-zj-ningbo-2026-mar:seve.overview: 文章谈幽默在科学传播中的作用：幽默能让艰深知识变好懂、提高受众参与、拉近科学家与公众的距离，但用错或用过头会误导受众、损害公信力，关键在于把握生动和严谨之间的平衡。
group:paper-mock-zj-ningbo-2026-mar:seve.fullTranslationZh:
人们喜爱幽默，因为它能点亮日常时刻、化解尴尬，让每一次交往都温暖而愉快。幽默的这种魔力不只在日常生活中起作用，在科学领域，尤其是在网络上，也同样大放异彩。一点幽默就能大大提升科学家的传播效果。

首先，幽默能把艰深的科学知识变简单。它能帮助普通人理解复杂的概念。例如，用“机器学习就像笨手笨脚的蹒跚学步的孩子”这样有趣的类比来解释自动驾驶汽车中的人工智能，能让非专业人群轻松理解抽象的概念。幽默还能有效提高受众的参与度。在社交媒体上分享实验室实验中巧妙幽默的故事的科学家，往往比枯燥的学术帖子获得更多互动。此外，幽默还能让科学家更有人情味，这一点在科普讲座中就能看到：轻松的笑话让听众觉得和研究人员更亲近。

不过，幽默在科学传播中是一把双刃剑。其中隐藏的风险值得我们注意。如果内容本身不真实，幽默甚至会取代事实，让受众仅凭自己看到的有趣帖子就对科学知识形成错误的看法。过度使用讽刺或负面的幽默也会适得其反，因为这会很快让科学家失去公众的信任，损害他们的公信力。

恰当地使用幽默，需要在生动的表达和专业的严谨之间取得平衡。它既不应盖过核心的科学信息，也不应浅薄到失去严肃性。用得过多会损害专业性。掌握这种平衡的科学家能有效缩小和公众之间的隔阂，让科学更亲切、更受欢迎。

completedSourceTexts.text: People favor humor, as it lights up daily moments, eases awkwardness and makes every interaction warm and enjoyable. This magic of humor doesn’t just work in daily life; it also shines in the field of science, especially online. A little humor can greatly enhance scientists’ communication effect.

Firstly, humor simplifies tough scientific knowledge. It’s a helper in making complex concepts understandable to ordinary people. For example, explaining AI in self-driving cars with a funny analogy about “machines learning like clumsy toddlers” makes abstract ideas easy for non-professional groups to understand. It also boosts audience engagement effectively. Scientists sharing clever and humorous stories about laboratory experiments on social media often attract more interactions than dry academic posts. Additionally, humor humanizes scientists, as seen in popular science lectures where light-hearted jokes help audiences feel closer to researchers.

Humor in scientific communication is a double-edged sword, though. The hidden risks deserve our attention. If the content itself is untrue, humor can even replace facts, leading the audience to form wrong opinions about scientific knowledge just based on the amusing posts they see. Overusing sarcasm or negative humor also has the opposite effect, as it will quickly make scientists lose the public’s trust and damage their credibility.

Proper humor use requires a balance between vivid expression and professional precision. It should neither overshadow the core scientific information nor be so shallow that it loses seriousness. Overuse harms professionalism. Scientists who master this balance can effectively narrow the divide with the public, making science more welcoming and popular.
